insights.claim: ogx-k8s-operator uses a two-tier controller architecture where the ogx-module controller deploys and manages the inner OGXServer operator via kustomize manifest rendering, enabling platform-specific overlay selection for ODH and RHOAI distributions.
insights.reasoning: The reconciler.go constants define separate overlays for ODH and RHOAI distributions (overlayODH, overlayRhoai), and the ogx-module controller watches the cluster-scoped OGX CR to manage the entire inner operator lifecycle. This two-tier pattern is a deliberate architectural choice that decouples the platform component management from the domain-specific OGXServer reconciliation.

insights.claim: The operator dynamically reads the OpenShift APIServer TLS profile at startup and applies platform-derived cipher suites to webhook and metrics servers, falling back to the Intermediate profile on non-OpenShift clusters.
insights.reasoning: The setupTLS function uses openshift/controller-runtime-common to fetch the TLS profile from the config.openshift.io/v1 APIServer resource. This ensures operator TLS configuration stays synchronized with the platform-wide TLS policy, including any FIPS-mandated cipher restrictions. The fallback to Intermediate profile makes the operator deployable on vanilla Kubernetes.

insights.claim: Neither Dockerfile.konflux uses GOEXPERIMENT=strictfipsruntime, so Go strict FIPS runtime enforcement is not active even though the PQC UBI base image and CGO dynamic linking are present.
insights.reasoning: While CGO_ENABLED=1 and the ubi-minimal-pqc base image ensure the binary is dynamically linked and OpenSSL is available, the absence of GOEXPERIMENT=strictfipsruntime means the Go runtime will not enforce FIPS-only crypto paths at runtime. The operator relies on platform TLS profiles for cipher selection but does not have a build-time guarantee against non-FIPS crypto usage within Go standard library internals.
